title: Your questions, answered
intro: Questions asked while building and testing FAST Studio, answered for this product as it is today. The newest question is at the top. Source: docs/faq/faq.json; rebuild with node tools/build-faq.mjs (also part of node tools/build-docs.mjs).

questions.question: Can I get a UI to manage the local R2, demo and production separately, like the R2 dashboard?
questions.short: Yes. Double-click r2.bat (production) or run "r2.bat demo". It opens Cloudflare's own Local Explorer, the R2 dashboard of Wrangler, on that environment's local R2: browse folders, upload files, add directories, download, delete (one or many) and see each file's details. "r2.bat stop" closes it. Before deleting, "node tools/r2-local.mjs --usage" shows which folders a video, ad or slate still uses.

sections.title: 1. Open it
sections.html:
r2.bat          # production (data-pilot\edge)
r2.bat demo     # demo (data\edge)
r2.bat stop     # close the explorers r2.bat started
  • If FAST Studio is running in that mode, the explorer of its edge opens (port 8787).
  • If not, r2.bat starts a browse-only edge for that environment (port 8798 production, 8797 demo; the first start can take a minute). start.bat closes it before starting FAST Studio, so two edges never share the same R2 folder.
  • The page also shows the edge's KV (the published channel schedules) and Durable Objects.

sections.title: 2. What you can do
sections.html:
• Browse: bucket fast-studio-media → folders _platform/ (slates) and one per project → one folder per video, ad or slate.
  • Upload files into the current folder, or Add directory.
  • Download or Delete a file from its details page; tick several rows to delete them together.
  • Images and videos are not previewed there: open http://127.0.0.1:8787/media/<key> (thumb.jpg in the browser, master.m3u8 in VLC).

sections.title: 3. Before deleting
sections.html:
node tools/r2-local.mjs --usage          # production (FAST Studio running in pilot mode)
node tools/r2-local.mjs --demo --usage   # demo (FAST Studio running in demo mode)

Each folder is marked IN USE (with the video, ad or slate) or unused, safe to delete. Deleting a folder that is in use breaks its playback (ads and slates live in R2 only). On 10 November 2026 production had three unused folders: the old platform slates (_platform/standby-5s, _platform/geo-5s, about 85 MB) and your archived first Big Buck Bunny upload.

The explorer itself doesn't know what FAST Studio uses, so it can't stop you; check first.

questions.question: How can I view the local R2 assets?
questions.short: On this PC, R2 is Wrangler's local stand-in. It keeps files as blobs plus a SQLite index under data-pilot/edge (production) or data/edge (demo), so they can't be browsed in Explorer. Run node tools/r2-local.mjs to list every folder (one per video, ad or slate) with its size and a link. Each link opens through the local edge at http://127.0.0.1:8787/media/…: images and playlists in the browser, videos in VLC.

sections.title: 1. List what is stored
sections.html:
node tools/r2-local.mjs                 # folders: files, size, date, master playlist link
node tools/r2-local.mjs arush-media/    # every file of a project (or any prefix)
node tools/r2-local.mjs --demo          # the demo's R2 instead of production's

It only reads the index, so it is safe while FAST Studio runs. On 10 November 2026 production held 5 folders, 417 files, about 608 MB: the two platform slates (old and six-level versions) and your uploaded video.

sections.title: 2. Open a file
sections.html:
• Thumbnail: open http://127.0.0.1:8787/media/<folder>/thumb.jpg in the browser.
  • Watch a video, ad or slate: in VLC, Media → Open Network Stream → paste the …/master.m3u8 link from the list (Chrome downloads playlists instead of playing them).
  • One segment: a …/seg_00000.ts link downloads a 5-second piece that VLC plays.

Folder names: <project slug>/<video id>.<revision>; inside, 0 … 5 are the quality levels (360p … 2160p) as MPEG-TS and f0 … f5 the fMP4 copies. _platform/… are the platform's slates.

sections.title: 3. In the cloud
sections.html: With real Cloudflare R2 you browse the same keys in the Cloudflare dashboard (R2 → the bucket fast-studio-media → Objects); download one with npx wrangler r2 object get fast-studio-media/<key> --remote --file out.ts. The edge address replaces 127.0.0.1:8787.

questions.question: How can I see my database and run manual queries?
questions.short: Production on this PC uses a built-in PostgreSQL 14 on 127.0.0.1, port 54339, database postgres, user postgres, no password (it only accepts connections from this PC). Connect any PostgreSQL tool to it, such as DBeaver or pgAdmin, and run queries. Tick "read-only" in the tool, because this login can change and delete everything for every tenant. To understand the tables first, open docs/html/visualizeDB.html.

sections.title: 1. Connection details
sections.html:
Production (pilot)Demo
Host127.0.0.1127.0.0.1
Port5433954329
Databasepostgrespostgres
Userpostgrespostgres
Passwordnone (local connections only)none
Filesdata-pilot/pgdata/pg

The database runs only while FAST Studio runs (it starts and stops with it). Checked on 9 November 2026: schema version V33.

sections.title: 2. With DBeaver (free, recommended)
sections.html:
1. Install DBeaver Community from dbeaver.io.
  2. Database → New Database Connection → PostgreSQL → Next.
  3. Host 127.0.0.1, Port 54339, Database postgres, Username postgres, Password empty.
  4. On the General page of the connection, tick Read-only connection.
  5. Test Connection (it downloads the driver the first time), Finish.
  6. Open postgres → Schemas → public → Tables to browse; SQL Editor → New SQL script to run queries.

pgAdmin and the VS Code "PostgreSQL" extension work with the same details.

sections.title: 3. Useful first queries
sections.html:
-- schema version
select version, description, installed_on from flyway_schema_history order by installed_rank desc limit 5;

-- projects (tenants' organizations)
select id, slug, name, kind from organization order by name;

-- videos of one project, newest first
select a.title, a.kind, a.status, a.status_detail, a.media_key, a.source_ref
from asset a join organization o on o.id = a.org_id
where o.slug = 'arush-media' order by a.created_at desc;

-- background jobs that failed
select kind, state, last_error, created_at from media_job where state = 'FAILED' order by created_at desc limit 20;

More ready-made diagnose queries, every table and what uses it: Database guide.

sections.title: 4. Be careful
sections.html:
• The postgres login is the database owner: it bypasses tenant isolation (row-level security) and sees and can change every tenant's data. Keep the connection read-only unless you mean to change something.
  • Before any manual change, take a backup: tools/backup.ps1 -Pilot (it stops the app for a consistent copy and starts it again).
  • Never change tables while FAST Studio is mid-way through a job, and never edit flyway_schema_history.
  • Stored credentials (Mux tokens, ad server tags) are encrypted; you will see ciphertext, not the secrets.

questions.question: I selected another quality in the player but it kept playing its own quality. Why?
questions.short: Fixed. The player changed quality only after everything it had already loaded ahead had played, and a short video is loaded completely at once, so it never changed. Now picking a quality switches at once: the picture changes within the current 5-second segment, and the badge under the player shows the new level.

sections.title: Details
sections.html:
• Video.js asks hls.js for the new level as its next level, which waits for the buffered video to run out.
  • FAST Studio now switches the level immediately (hls.js currentLevel), which drops what was loaded ahead and loads the chosen level.
  • Auto goes back to picking by connection speed and player size; a small player starts at a lower level.

questions.question: I uploaded a file to Mux from our platform, but the video still said "Waiting for Source Video File". Why?
questions.short: The upload had worked: the file went to Mux, and Mux was still converting it. The drawer showed the wrong message for that wait. It now says "Converting in your video library", and the Library refreshes by itself until the video is ready (usually a few minutes after the upload).

sections.title: What happens after an upload to the video library
sections.html:
1. The browser sends the file straight to Mux.
  2. Mux converts it (a few minutes, longer for long or 4K files). The video shows Converting in your video library.
  3. FAST Studio checks every 20 seconds (or gets Mux's webhook), links the Mux video, reads its quality levels and segments, and marks it Ready.

questions.question: Uploads should go to the tenant's connected connector (ask which one when there are several); slate and ads should be separate from media, uploaded only in the Ads section, and stored and served from R2 only.
questions.short: Done. The Library holds programmes only and uploads them to the connected video library (you choose when there are several). Ad creatives and your own slate are added under Ads; FAST Studio converts them once, copies them to R2 and then deletes its own copy of the video files, so they are served from R2 only.

sections.title: 1. Library: programmes only
sections.html:
• Add video offers programme types only (movies, episodes, shorts); ad creatives no longer appear in the Library.
  • Uploads go straight to the connected video library; with several, Upload to asks which. The names shown are the ones the platform administrator gave the connections; one still named after its platform shows as "Video library", so projects never see the platform's name.
  • Platform administrators can add more than one Mux connection to a project in the connector marketplace (tenant page → Connectors).

sections.title: 2. Ads section: creatives and slate
sections.html:
• Ad creatives: Add creative (upload or generate), list, and the detail drawer. Campaigns pick their creative from these.
  • Slate: upload your own short loop (10 to 60 s, no speech). Once converted, your channels show it instead of the platform's "We'll be right back" screen, for unfilled ad time, schedule gaps and unreachable programmes. "Use platform standby" brings the platform screen back. The region-block screen stays the platform's.

sections.title: 3. R2 only
sections.html:
• FAST Studio converts the ad or slate into the tenant's quality levels (MPEG-TS and fMP4), copies everything to R2, and once R2 confirms both copies it deletes its own video files and the uploaded original.
  • It keeps only the playlists and thumbnail (a few KB) as an index: segment counts and quality levels are read from them.
  • Channels play ads and slate from R2 through the edge. Previews in the Ads section load the playlists from FAST Studio and the video segments are redirected to the edge (R2).
  • The platform's own standby and region-block slates live in R2 only too.

questions.question: I added a video in the Library with Upload, but it did not go to Mux. Where did it go, and how is it playing?
questions.short: Since 9 November 2026 (later the same day), Library → Add video → Upload sends the file straight to the project's connected video library (Mux today), never through FAST Studio. With more than one library connected you choose which one. Only a project without a video library uploads to FAST Studio. Videos uploaded before this change stay on FAST Studio storage and keep playing from there.

sections.title: 1. Where an upload goes now
sections.html:
• Project with a video library: the browser sends the file straight to the library (one-time upload link). The library converts it; FAST Studio links the video when it is ready (by webhook, or by checking every 20 seconds when webhooks can't reach the server) and then streams it from the library like a synced video.
  • Several libraries (e.g. two Mux accounts): Add video shows Upload to; pick one. Each video remembers its library, and sync, streaming and signed links use that one.
  • No video library: the file goes to FAST Studio, which converts it and keeps it in R2.
  • Ads and slate are never sent to the video library (see the next question).

sections.title: 2. The video you uploaded earlier
sections.html: It was uploaded before this change, so it stays where it is: original under data-pilot/uploads/…, converted copy under data-pilot/media/arush-media/… and in R2 (the local stand-in under data-pilot/edge). It keeps playing from there. To move it into Mux, upload the file again with Add video, then archive the old one.

questions.question: Can we use a JavaScript video player instead of the plain HTML one, with quality selection in the player, the video title on it and more controls, everywhere a video plays?
questions.short: Yes, done. Every player in FAST Studio (Library video detail, Watch live, and the Partner page's "Try it as a viewer") now uses Video.js 10 with hls.js. It shows the title on the video and has a ⚙ Settings menu with Quality (Auto or a fixed level) and Speed, plus picture-in-picture, fullscreen, casting, volume and keyboard shortcuts.

sections.title: 1. Where it is used
sections.html:
• Library → a Ready video: title = the video's title. Clicking a break in the ad-break timeline still jumps the player there. A badge under it says which level is playing.
  • Watch live: title = the channel name. The badge above the player now shows the real level playing (it used to show a fixed "1080p60").
  • Partner → a shared channel → Stream → Try it as a viewer: title = the channel name.

sections.title: 2. Controls
sections.html:
• Play/pause, seek bar with time, volume, ⚙ Settings (Quality, Speed), cast, picture-in-picture, fullscreen.
  • Quality lists the levels the stream offers (the tenant's quality levels). Auto picks by connection speed and shows the level it picked, e.g. "Auto (720p)".
  • Keyboard shortcuts for play/pause, seeking, volume, mute and fullscreen.
  • Live channels start muted (browsers block sound on autoplay); press the speaker to unmute.

sections.title: 3. How it works
sections.html:
• One shared component, frontend/src/shared/Player.tsx, built from @videojs/react (VideoPlayer + VideoSkin) and @videojs/hlsjs-video. Pages use VideoPlayer from shared/ui.tsx.
  • The player is downloaded only when a page shows a video (about 250 kB compressed, including hls.js).
  • It keeps what the old player did: HLS interstitial events for client-side ads (SGAI) and their beacons on Watch live, and on a fatal error a "Playback problem … Retrying…" badge, a reload after 3 s for network errors, and media-error recovery.
  • Safari and iPhone use their own HLS playback through the same player.

questions.question: Can every quality level be configured per tenant from platform admin, and how do I see which level is playing in the video detail player?
questions.short: Yes. On the tenant page → Configuration → Quality levels, a platform administrator ticks any of 360p, 540p, 720p, 1080p, 1440p (2K) and 2160p (4K). That tenant's uploads and ads are converted to exactly those levels and its channels offer them. In the Library, the video's detail player has a Quality menu (⚙ Settings on the player → Quality: Auto or a fixed level) and a badge under it saying which level is playing.

sections.title: 1. Setting the levels (platform administrators)
sections.html:
1. Platform administration → Tenants → the tenant → Configuration (scope: Tenant defaults).
  2. Tick the levels in Quality levels; the card shows the storage per hour of video at your choice (e.g. about 3.9 GB for 720p + 1080p, about 8 GB for 4K alone).
  3. Save quality levels. New conversions use them within 30 seconds.

Only platform administrators can change this (a tenant owner gets "Only the platform administrator may change this setting"), because higher levels cost encoding time, storage and delivery. The default is 360p, 540p and 720p. It applies to the whole tenant, every project.

sections.title: 2. What changes when you save
sections.html:
• Uploads and ads converted after the change get exactly the chosen levels (one folder per level: 0 = 360p … 5 = 2160p) and an fMP4 copy of each. Existing videos are not converted again.
  • Channels offer the chosen levels. Where a video or ad lacks a level (converted before the change), that level plays its nearest lower one, so nothing breaks.
  • Slates carry all six levels, so they fit every tenant.
  • Mux videos keep the levels Mux made; each channel level plays the Mux level nearest in height. Uploads through FAST Studio ask Mux for the 1440p or 2160p tier when the tenant uses those levels (Mux charges more for them).
  • A small source (say 720p) is scaled up to every chosen level; it does not gain detail.

sections.title: 3. Seeing and choosing the level in the player
sections.html:
1. Library → click a Ready video. On the player, ⚙ Settings → Quality; under the player, a badge with the level playing.
  2. Auto lets the player choose by connection speed; the menu shows which level Auto picked, e.g. "Auto (720p)".
  3. Pick a level (e.g. "1080p · 5.8 Mbit/s") to force it; the badge changes to e.g. "Playing 1080p · 1920×1080 · 5.8 Mbit/s" once the switch is done.
  4. "2 levels in this video" tells you how many levels the video actually has; for a Mux video these are Mux's levels.

sections.title: 4. Checked on 9 November 2026
sections.html: On a separate production-mode copy: a tenant set to 720p + 1080p; a new video was converted to exactly those (folders 2 and 3, plus fMP4 copies); the player listed both and switched; a live channel offered "720p, 1080p" and its 720p and 1080p playlists used folders 2 and 3, every file downloadable.

questions.question: Do we support 4K or 2K?
questions.short: Not yet. FAST Studio plays at most 720p today, and your Mux video only has levels up to 1080p. Mux itself can make 2K/2.5K (1440p) and 4K (2160p) levels, but only for videos you upload with a higher resolution tier, which costs more. To play them, FAST Studio would first need 1080p, then 1440p and 2160p levels for its own ads and slate, or accept a lower picture during breaks.

sections.title: 1. What exists today
sections.html:
Highest level
FAST Studio (uploads, ads, slate, and what the live playlist offers)720p
Your Mux video "Songs Mashup 2010"1080p (two bitrates)
Mux in general, on-demand videoup to 2160p (4K), if the video is created with a higher max_resolution_tier

sections.title: 2. Mux and 2K/4K
sections.html:
• Mux makes 1080p at most unless told otherwise: the default max_resolution_tier is 1080p, so a 4K source still becomes 1080p.
  • For 2K/2.5K set "max_resolution_tier": "1440p", for 4K "2160p", when the video is created or uploaded. FAST Studio's direct upload doesn't set it today; videos uploaded in the Mux dashboard can.
  • Higher tiers cost more for encoding, storage and delivery. It isn't clear that the free plan covers them; check Mux's pricing page before testing.

sections.title: 3. What FAST Studio would need
sections.html:
1. A 1080p level first for ads, slate and uploads, so viewers get Mux's 1080p without the picture dropping at each break. Moderate work; more conversion time and storage per ad.
  2. For 2K/4K: 1440p/2160p levels for ads and slate as well, or let breaks play at 1080p inside a 4K channel (a visible quality drop at each break, but most ad creatives are 1080p anyway). 4K delivery is roughly 15–25 Mbit/s per viewer, so Mux delivery costs rise accordingly. 4K is often HEVC (H.265), which needs fMP4 (already supported) and players that can decode it; the live playlist would also have to declare HEVC.

Suggested order: 1080p now, 2K/4K only when a customer asks for it.

questions.question: What renditions does our platform support, and which did Mux give?
questions.short: FAST Studio makes and plays three quality levels: 360p, 540p and 720p. Mux gave your video "Songs Mashup 2010" five: 360p, 540p, 720p and two 1080p. Viewers get Mux's 360p, 540p and 720p (each of our levels takes the Mux level nearest in height); Mux's two 1080p levels are not used yet, because our ads and slate only go up to 720p.

sections.title: 1. FAST Studio's quality levels
sections.html:
Every video FAST Studio converts (uploads, generated samples, ads, slate) gets the same three levels, so playback can switch between programme, ad and slate at any 5-second piece:

LevelPictureVideo bitrateDeclared to players
360p640×360600 kbit/s0.8 Mbit/s
540p960×5401,400 kbit/s1.7 Mbit/s
720p1280×7202,500 kbit/s2.9 Mbit/s

All: H.264 (Main profile), 25 frames a second, a keyframe at every 5 s, AAC stereo audio at 96 kbit/s, loudness −23 LUFS. Each is stored as MPEG-TS and, since 9 November 2026, also as an fMP4 copy. Defined in MediaServiceV1.LADDER.

sections.title: 2. What Mux gave for your video
sections.html:
Read from production's database (table asset_playback) on 9 November 2026:

Mux levelPictureBitrate (Mux)Used by FAST Studio?
1080p1920×10803.9 Mbit/sNo
1080p1920×10802.9 Mbit/sNo
720p1280×7201.5 Mbit/sYes, for our 720p
540p960×5400.97 Mbit/sYes, for our 540p
360p640×3600.50 Mbit/sYes, for our 360p

Format fMP4 (CMAF), public playback (not signed). 291 pieces: 290 of exactly 5.000 s and a last one of 4.286 s, 24 min 14.3 s in total. In the schedule it takes 24 min 15 s (whole 5-second slots); the last 0.7 s are slate. Mux decides its levels from your source file (here a 1080p source), and adds a second, higher-bitrate 1080p level.

sections.title: 3. How the two are matched
sections.html:
• The live playlist offers players our three levels. For each, the edge Worker takes the Mux level with the nearest height (on a tie, the lower one): 360p→360p, 540p→540p, 720p→720p.
  • During the programme the player gets Mux's pieces for that level; during breaks our ad and slate pieces of the same level, so the picture size stays the same across the join.
  • A different source gives different Mux levels (e.g. a 720p upload gives no 1080p). Matching by height still works; a channel never offers more than our 720p.

sections.title: 4. Things to know
sections.html:
• No 1080p yet. To offer Mux's 1080p, FAST Studio must add a 1080p level for ads and slate (and uploads) first, otherwise the picture would drop at every break. Not built; listed as left in the test guide.
  • Declared bitrates are ours. The live playlist tells players our figures (e.g. 2.9 Mbit/s for 720p) while Mux's 720p is about 1.5 Mbit/s, so players on slow connections may pick a lower level than they could. Harmless, but could be tuned per channel later.
  • Codec profile. Ours is H.264 Main; Mux may use High. Players switch at each source change (there is a discontinuity marker), which web, iOS and Android TV players handle; still part of the real-device test.

questions.question: I synced Mux and my video got ready after "transcoding". Where is my video stored in the system, and how is it playing?
questions.short: Your Mux video is stored only in Mux. FAST Studio never downloads or converts it: "getting it ready" only reads its playlists and records how it is cut (quality levels and the length of every piece). When someone watches, our edge Worker writes a live playlist that sends the player to Mux for the programme and to our own storage (R2) for ads and slate.

boxes: Stores your video and serves its pieces (stream.mux.com / Mux CDN)
Remembers the video's details, the schedule and the ads; never serves video
Writes each viewer's live playlist every few seconds
Our ads and slate, converted once by FFmpeg
Downloads programme pieces from Mux, ad and slate pieces from R2

sections.title: 1. What each step did
sections.html:
1. Sync asked Mux for its list of videos and added each one to the Library as a Draft. Only a catalogue entry was created: title, length and a link to the Mux video (mux:<Mux asset id>).
  2. Get ready to stream (or Retry processing) is not a transcode for Mux videos, even though the screen used to call it that. FAST Studio asked Mux for the video's playlists and recorded: its playback ID, whether playback is signed, the container (fMP4 in your case), the quality levels (e.g. 360p, 720p) and the exact length of every ~5-second piece. That takes a few seconds and copies nothing. The video is then Ready.
  3. Your video's Delivery card shows exactly this: Streams from: Video library (not copied), the number of pieces, the quality levels and the format.

sections.title: 2. Where things are stored
sections.html:
WhatWhere
The video itself (every quality level, every piece)Mux only: Mux's storage, delivered by Mux's CDN. Nothing of it is in FAST Studio, R2 or on this PC.
Its catalogue entry (title, length, licence, ad break points)FAST Studio's database: table asset, plus asset_source (which Mux video it is and what Mux last said about it). On this PC the production database is in data-pilot\pg.
How it streams (playback ID, signed or not, fMP4/TS, quality levels, piece lengths)Same database, table asset_playback. No video addresses or tokens are stored; signed links are made when needed.
Your Mux access token and signing keySame database, encrypted (table connector_value). Never shown again after you save them.
Ads and slate ("We'll be right back", "Not available in your region")Converted once by FFmpeg into 5-second pieces (MPEG-TS and an fMP4 copy) in data-pilot\media, then copied to the edge storage: Cloudflare R2 in real hosting, data-pilot\edge on this PC (the local Worker stands in for R2).
Videos you upload straight to FAST Studio (not via Mux)Converted by FFmpeg like ads, in data-pilot\media and R2. Only these are stored by FAST Studio.
The schedule as the edge sees itA "snapshot" the server sends to the edge every few seconds when something changes (edge key-value storage; data-pilot\edge on this PC). For your Mux video it holds the Mux playlist address, the piece lengths and where each programme starts and ends.

sections.title: 3. How it plays, step by step
sections.html:
1. You schedule the video on a channel, publish and press Go Live. The server writes the channel's snapshot to the edge.
  2. A viewer opens the channel (Watch live, VLC, Safari, a TV app). They get an address on the edge Worker, not on the FAST Studio server.
  3. Every few seconds the player asks the Worker for the live playlist. The Worker works it out from the snapshot and the clock: which programme or break is on now.
  4. For your Mux programme the Worker reads Mux's own playlist once per location and quality level (then reuses it for every viewer) and lists Mux's piece addresses at their real lengths.
  5. At an ad break it lists our pieces instead: ads chosen live for that viewer (your campaigns first, then ad servers such as Google Ad Manager), and slate for any time no ad fills. A marker (EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY) tells the player the source changes; for fMP4 each source also gets its own start header (EXT-X-MAP).
  6. The player downloads programme pieces directly from Mux and ad/slate pieces from R2 through Cloudflare's CDN. The FAST Studio server sends no video at all; it only answers "which ads for this break".
  7. If Mux can't be reached, the Worker plays slate for the programme's length and returns to Mux when it can; the channel never stops.

sections.title: 4. See it for yourself
sections.html:
• Library → your video → Delivery card: "Video library (not copied)", pieces, quality levels, fMP4.
  • Watch live → Live HLS Manifest Inspector: the playlist the player gets. During the programme the addresses point at Mux; during breaks at the edge (…/media/…), with EXT-X-MAP headers for fMP4.
  • docs/html/visualizeDB.html: the tables asset, asset_source and asset_playback.
  • Folder data-pilot\media: you will find the slates and any ads or uploads, but no folder for your Mux video.

sections.title: 5. What it means for cost
sections.html: Mux bills for viewing minutes of your programmes (its free plan covers 100,000 minutes a month). Ads and slate come from R2, which charges nothing for data sent to viewers. Keeping Mux videos out of R2 was your decision on 3 November 2026 (docs/OVP_DELIVERY_PLAN.md).
